newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Issue Dept fx assets fall by 51 mln marks.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Issue Dept fx assets fall by 51 mln marks.

text.p: Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) Issue Department foreign exchange assets fell to the lev equivalent of 3.478 billion marks on August 15 from 3.529 billion marks a week earlier, BNB figures showed on Monday.
BNB officials declined to comment on the reasons for the fall.

Under an IMF-prescribed currency board system introduced on July 1 the lev was pegged at 1,000 per mark as an anchor currency and the BNB pledged to buy and sell unlimited volumes of marks at 995 levs bid and 1,000 ask.

The currency board bans the BNB from lending to the government and commercial banks and requires levs in circulation to be fully matched by the Issue Department's assets, which make up the BNB foreign exchange reserves.
Cash and correspondent bank accounts in foreign currencies fell to the lev equivalent of 1.437 billion marks on August 15 from 1.520 billion marks on August 8.
But BNB holdings in foreign securities rose to 1.393 trillion levs from 1.360 trillion levs, figures showed.
Issue Department assets included 640.7 billion levs in monetary gold and 7.7 billion levs in accrued interest receivable as of August 15.
Any rise in the Issue Department assets allows for a limited rise of the lev currency in circulation without accumulating inflationary pressure under the currency board.
Under the BNB law the market value of the assets, denominated in foreign currency other than the mark, has been limited to two percent of the total BNB liabilities denominated in the same currency.
So far there are no official figures on BNB operations to transfer part of dollar reserves into mark-denominated assets.
Currency in circulation, part of the Issue Department liabilities, rose to 953.8 billion levs on August 15 from 882.2 billion levs on August 8.
The department's liabilities also included 618.8 billion levs in bank deposits and current accounts on August 15, down from 696.5 billion levs a week earlier.
Since July 14, when the BNB halted interest payments on banks' current accounts at the BNB, local banks have pared their holdings in those accounts.
The State Fund for Reconstruction and Development account, also part of the department's liabilities, fell to 584.2 billion levs on August 15 from 628.6 billion levs on August 8.
Government deposits and accounts, a liability of the Issue Department, rose to 516.6 billion levs from 503.1 billion levs on August 8.
The liabilities also included a 790.4 billion lev deposit of the BNB Banking Department on August 15, a fall by 13.3 billion levs from the week before.

Under the currency board system the Banking Department is the lender of last resort for local commercial banks. It can extend refinancing to sound banks only in case of systemic risk for the banking and payments system.
